title: Sell Mineral Rights in Penn, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Penn, PA
metaDescription: Penn, Westmoreland County mineral rights owner? We buy oil and gas interests along the Loyalhanna corridor, straight answers, fair cash offers.
heroLead: Penn sits along the Loyalhanna Creek corridor in Westmoreland County, a small borough surrounded by the kind of rolling farmland that made this part of the state attractive to gas operators once wet-gas Marcellus development moved east from the Washington County core.
intro: We hear from Penn-area families in two very different situations: some have an active lease with years of royalty history and want to know what that stream is worth as a lump sum, and others hold minerals that have sat unleased through the entire boom and are wondering whether that's ever going to change. Both situations are ones we can put a real number to.

sections.heading: Leased Versus Unleased Value Near Penn
paragraphs: An active lease with production history gives us the clearest basis for an offer, since we can look at actual royalty payments and current well performance rather than estimating. If your Penn tract has been under lease for several years, we'll ask for recent statements so we can price against real numbers instead of a general Westmoreland County range.

Unleased minerals are harder to value precisely, but not impossible — we look at leasing and drilling activity on nearby tracts to estimate what your interest would likely command if it were leased today, then build our offer around that.

sections.heading: Working Around Complicated Family Ownership
paragraphs: A number of the older farm tracts around Penn have been divided among children and grandchildren over the decades, sometimes without every transfer being recorded promptly at the Westmoreland County recorder of deeds in Greensburg. We handle that kind of title cleanup directly and explain in plain language what, if anything, your family needs to do before a sale can close.

faqs.question: What documents do I need to get started?
faqs.answer: A copy of your deed if you have it helps, but if not, we can locate the recorded version through the Westmoreland County courthouse ourselves.

faqs.question: Can you buy just part of my interest, not all of it?
faqs.answer: In most cases, yes, we can structure an offer for a portion of your interest if you'd rather not sell the whole thing.

faqs.question: How is an unleased interest priced differently from a leased one?
faqs.answer: Leased interests with royalty history give us concrete numbers to work from; unleased interests are priced against nearby leasing and drilling activity instead.

faqs.question: Will I need to travel to Greensburg to sign anything?
faqs.answer: No, we handle closing by mail or courier for most Penn-area sellers, and notarization can usually be done locally rather than requiring a trip to the courthouse.
